title: Specificity and selector complexity review
learningObjectives: Explain specificity and selector complexity review and use selectors or sizing rules appropriately.

understand.concept: Specificity is one part of the cascade used to resolve competing declarations. Selector complexity can increase specificity and make later overrides difficult. The :where() pseudo-class can group selectors without adding specificity; :is() and :not() take specificity from their most specific argument, while :has() follows its argument specificity rules.
understand.whyItMatters: A stylesheet that relies on highly specific selectors becomes harder to maintain. Prefer clear component classes, deliberate cascade layers, and small selector scopes over escalating specificity.
understand.analogy: Specificity is a priority score within the cascade, but selector complexity is also a maintenance cost.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the idea; selector matching and sizing follow CSS specifications and browser layout algorithms.

explain.narrative: The ID-based rule wins the colour conflict. The :where() portion contributes zero specificity to the later selector.

questions.prompt: Which selector strategy usually makes component styles easier to maintain?
questions.explanation: Clear and reasonably low-specificity selectors reduce accidental cascade conflicts.
